submitLabel: Your transcript excerpts, documentation, and reflection
intro: Paste the relevant transcript excerpts (M4 rules apply — nothing person-identifying), your catch documentation, and the 250–350 word reflection ending with your team rule. Resubmission is free and unlimited — the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext:
You are grading a learner submission for an AI fluency course for People leaders (AI 101, The Foundation). Module 6 applied activity, 'Catch It Lying': the learner fished for a hallucination in a domain where they hold real expertise, asking questions without supplying material; caught a confident wrong claim (or documented honest declines/hedges — which the activity explicitly counts as valid data); proved wrongness against a named real source; classified the failure by type (fabricated specifics / plausible-but-wrong reasoning / confident gaps / stale facts) and named the tell that should catch it; compared attempt count against their prediction; and wrote a one-sentence verification rule for their team. A numeric prediction may have been captured by the module's opening calibration prompt; grade the calibration dimension on whether the prediction is stated and honestly compared, never on its accuracy. A submission reporting that the model declined to fabricate, documented honestly with attempts shown, can score full marks on every dimension — the calibration lesson stands either way.

**"Our evidence cannot settle this" scores at full credit where it is the honest answer.** A submission that states plainly what its evidence cannot establish, and why, has done the exercise correctly — never mark it down for declining to reach a conclusion its evidence does not support. Reaching a confident conclusion on thin evidence is the error; naming the limit is the skill.

opening.label: Predicted — attempts before you catch one
opening.hint: Each distinct question is one attempt. Honest declines count as attempts.

calibration.label: Actual — attempts it took (or total attempts, if it never invented)
calibration.hint: Way fewer than predicted = you've been over-trusting. Way more = your expectations are stale.

dimensions.name: The ground is real expertise
dimensions.criteria: The domain is one they demonstrably own, and wrongness is proven against a named source — a policy section, a statute, a system of record — not just 'I know this is wrong.' The proof is specific enough that a colleague could re-verify it.

dimensions.name: The fishing is diagnostic
dimensions.criteria: Questions aimed where the types live — specifics, org particulars, time-sensitive details — with material deliberately withheld, attempts counted, and hedges or declines recorded as data rather than skipped. Random questions that happened to work score lower than aimed ones.

dimensions.name: The catch is classified
dimensions.criteria: The wrong claim captured exactly, the truth stated, the failure typed correctly, and the tell named — the one that should have caught it in the wild. A near-miss classification with visible reasoning outscores a correct label with none.

dimensions.name: The rule and the calibration
dimensions.criteria: The team rule is one enforceable sentence aimed at the type they caught — followable by a person, auditable by another. 'Be careful with AI' fails this dimension. Prediction compared, direction named, and the honest sentence about their own trust calibration written.
